challenge.method: Tested the definition against a dataset for which applicable law provides no database right and a database containing third-party material. Traced whose rights the Statement of Purpose and sections 2–4 address.
challenge.results: Where applicable law provides no database right, section 1 creates none. For third-party material, the Statement of Purpose qualifies the Affirmer’s action by ownership. The section 2 waiver and section 3 fallback reach only the Affirmer’s rights, and section 4(c) disclaims responsibility for clearing others’ rights. Inclusion in the definition supplies no dedication by another rights holder.

limitations: Protection of a particular database, ownership of rights in it or its contents, and the legal effectiveness of a waiver each require evidence beyond the definition.
reasoning: Section 1 says a Work “may be protected” and gives a nonexclusive definition of Copyright and Related Rights. Item (v) expressly includes rights protecting extraction, dissemination, use and reuse of data in a Work. Item (vi) separately includes database rights and gives the EU directive as an example.
